stem: A client asks whether the legal requirements for an advance directive are identical in every U.S. state. Which response is most accurate?

options.A: No. Providers must inform patients about advance-directive rights under the law of the state in which care is furnished
options.B: Yes. Federal law creates one identical execution form and witness rule for every state
options.C: State law is irrelevant to advance directives in Medicare-participating hospitals
options.D: Advance directives are valid only if a hospital writes them for the patient

rationale: Federal requirements at 42 CFR 489.102 require covered providers to give adults written information about their rights under applicable state law to make medical decisions and formulate advance directives, and to comply with state-law requirements. Therefore, execution and related requirements are not appropriately described as nationally identical.
educational_objective: Recognize that advance-directive requirements are governed in part by applicable state law and must be explained accordingly.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services / eCFR
source_document_title: 42 CFR §489.102 — Requirements for Providers: Advance Directives
source_claim_supported: Supports written information about state-law rights concerning advance directives and compliance with state-law requirements.
correction_summary: Retained the state-variation concept but anchored it to the exact federal rule instead of a generic POLST source.
audit_findings: A follows the federal regulation; B/C deny state-law variation and D misstates who formulates directives.
